findings.title: KeyError when integration metadata lacks 'sender' key
findings.body: The expression `integration.metadata["sender"]["login"]` will raise a `KeyError` if the integration's metadata does not contain a "sender" key. In `build_integration`, the "sender" key is only added conditionally (`if state.get("sender")`), so any integration created without sender information (e.g., older installations or those created via a different path) will cause an unhandled 500 error when a user attempts to reinstall or when this code path is reached. This should use `.get()` with a fallback or check for key existence before accessing.

findings.title: Unhandled exception from get_user_info can cause 500 error
findings.body: `get_user_info(payload["access_token"])` is called without any exception handling. If the GitHub API returns an error, times out, or the access token is invalid in a way that causes an exception (rather than a response without 'login'), the user will see a raw 500 error instead of the graceful error page. This call should be wrapped in a try/except that returns the same `error(request, self.active_organization)` response on failure.

findings.title: redirect_uri is not URL-encoded in the OAuth authorize URL
findings.body: The `redirect_uri` value is interpolated directly into the query string without URL-encoding: `f"...&redirect_uri={redirect_uri}"`. Since `redirect_uri` is a full URL (e.g., `http://testserver/extensions/github/setup/`), characters like `:`, `/` should be percent-encoded per RFC 6749 Section 3.1.2. Some OAuth providers or intermediary proxies may reject or misparse the request. Use `urllib.parse.quote` or `urlencode` to properly encode the parameter.

findings.title: OAuth state parameter compared with non-constant-time equality
findings.body: The state parameter (used as CSRF protection in the OAuth flow) is compared using `!=` which is not constant-time. While the practical exploitability over a network is low, security best practice for comparing secret or token-like values is to use `hmac.compare_digest()` to prevent timing side-channel attacks.

findings.title: Webhook HMAC signature likely does not match modified payload
findings.body: In `test_github_user_mismatch`, the webhook event payload is modified (`webhook_event["sender"]["login"] = "attacker"`) but the HMAC signature `sha1=d184e6717f8bfbcc291ebc8c0756ee446c6c9486` is hardcoded from the original `INSTALLATION_EVENT_EXAMPLE`. If webhook signature verification is enforced, this request should be rejected with a 403, not return 204. Either the signature needs to be recomputed for the modified payload, or the test is not actually exercising the intended code path (the integration may be created via a different mechanism than assumed).
